summary.title: Mid-Term Summary, Fall 2026 Term
summary.note: Weeks 1 to 8 of 16. Attendance through Friday, August 28, 2026. Student survey collected in class August 24 to 28, 70 responses from 100 enrolled.
summary.lead: 13 of the 73 students still attending enrolled in the last two weeks. Of the 87 who started in July, 60 are still coming. 27 have stopped, and 17 of those have no logged contact.

blocks.heading: WHAT THE ATTENDANCE SHOWS
items: Program attendance fell from 79% in week 1 to 67% in week 8. Almost all of that decline sits in the two evening classes.
Evening classes went from 73% in weeks 1 to 4 down to 56% in weeks 5 to 8, and to 44% in week 8. Morning classes moved 3 points over the same period.
Retention splits the same way. Morning classes are holding 84% of their students. Evening classes are holding 55%.
The break falls between week 6 and week 7, which is when the K-12 school year started. 15 of the 27 students who left were already gone by week 4.
13 new students started in weeks 7 and 8. The roster still looks close to full, which hides the loss.

blocks.heading: WHAT STUDENTS WROTE
items: One survey item scores badly, and only in two classes. "The class schedule works for my life": GED Evening 2.25, ESL Intermediate 2.64. Every other class is 3.94 or higher.
Those same students rate the class itself well. GED Evening gives 4.33 on "met my expectations" and 4.08 on "would tell a friend to come here."

Childcare and the start of the school year is the most named barrier, given by 18 students, including 8 of the 12 in GED Evening. Transportation is next at 13, and three GED Evening students named the last bus specifically.
"I know what I need to do to reach my goal" is the weakest item program-wide at 3.63. GED Morning sits at 3.31, with 12 of 16 answering exactly neutral. Healthcare Bridge is the exception at 4.54.
Healthcare Bridge students describe being able to see where they are on a plan. Their requests are about cost: 7 of 13 named scrubs or the CNA test fee.
Read the survey with care. It was given in class, so the 27 students who already left are not in it, and response rates were lowest in GED Evening (60%) and ESL Intermediate (61%).

table.data: 55% still attending, 62% attendance, 41% in week 8. Schedule score 2.25. Nine students gone, five with no logged contact.
table.decide: Decide: add a daytime or Saturday section, move the end time to 8:30, or both.

table.data: 56% still attending, week 8 at 47%. Zero logged contacts across 18 students, and 4 of the 8 who left have no contact on file.
table.decide: Decide: who calls an absent student, how fast, and where it gets written down.

table.data: Attendance is steady at 73%, but goal clarity is the lowest in the program and 4 students asked for a practice test or a test date.
table.decide: Decide: what goes in writing for each student, and by when.

table.data: 88% still attending, 85% attendance, highest scores on belonging and goal clarity in the program.
table.decide: Decide: which piece of this another class copies, and whether we can cover scrubs and the CNA test fee.

blocks2.heading: WHAT WE COULD TRY IN THE SECOND HALF
items: Add a daytime or Saturday section. Nine students asked for one in the survey, six of them in the evening classes, and three more have it written in their attendance notes.
End GED Evening at 8:30 instead of 9:00. Three students said that alone would let them catch the last bus.
Call any student who misses two sessions in a row, within 48 hours, and log it in the Last Contact column. 12 students have a logged call and 11 of the 12 are still attending.
Give every GED Morning student a written plan with a practice test date and a target test date on it.
Price out scrubs and CNA test fee help for Healthcare Bridge, and bus passes for the students who named transportation.
Check the 22 students under 12 contact hours before the term ends. 10 have already left. 12 are recent starts who can still get there.

blocks2.heading: QUESTIONS FOR YOUR TEACHERS
items: Which of your students who stopped coming would come back to a morning or Saturday section? Name them, so we can size the section before we build it.
What is our rule right now for calling an absent student, who does it, and where does it get written down? Logged contact runs from 0% of students in one class to 33% in another.
Which students in your class are one or two absences away from being at risk, and what do you already know about why?
GED Morning: what does each student still need before they can sit for the test, and can we put that on paper for them this month?
Healthcare Bridge: what do you do that makes students say they can see where they are on a plan? Which piece of it could another class run?
What would you need from me to make two-absence call-backs happen? Time, a phone, a printed list, or something else?
Does anything here not match what you see in the room, and where is the attendance data wrong?
